item.title: More school districts are shrinking. New research asks whether closures work
item.description: School districts across the country are closing campuses as enrollment falls. New research says the financial savings may be smaller than expected.

item.description: The FAA's response to a deadly crash is opening a larger debate about staffing, safety and a workplace practice controllers call the "early shove."

item.title: ICE arrests are surging as the administration targets more immigrants
item.description: ICE made nearly 50,000 arrests in July -- the highest monthly total of Trump's second term -- as enforcement expands to more places like airports, courthouses and immigration check-ins.

item.description: Maine's lobster fishing industry is closely integrated with processors across the border in Canada. People who depend on it are feeling whiplash from on-again, off-again tariff threats.

item.description: People have been avoiding lettuce this summer. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Washington Post columnist Tamar Haspel, who says we really should just skip the lettuce, permanently.

item.title: Why is one WNBA team calling in national security experts?
item.description: The WNBA's popularity has risen in recent years, but so have threats and abuse directed at its players. One team is taking a novel approach to this, by partnering with national security specialists.

item.title: How America celebrated and mourned Dolly Parton, in Nashville and beyond
item.description:
The great Dolly Parton died earlier this week and tributes have poured in from across the country.

Fans are mourning the loss of a country music icon who not only changed the musical landscape but gave back to communities with her Imagination Library program and donations to develop the Moderna COVID vaccine.
